findings.governingReading: The wind makes the exposed body simultaneously rust and scorch away.
findings.explanation: The English drops the burning component.

findings.highlight: How long will I stay here?
findings.evidenceJa: どのくらい長く“此処”にいるのか
findings.governingReading: The perceiver cannot tell how long he has already existed in this place.
findings.explanation: The English changes elapsed duration into a question about the future.

findings.governingReading: The dream presents a time that literally contains no time.
findings.explanation: The English rationalizes the contradiction as subjective loss of time sense.

findings.governingReading: The body is exposed to the wind for an impossibly long span.
findings.explanation: The English promotes long duration into eternity.

findings.governingReading: The dream drives the perceiver forward before restating the suffering of the place.
findings.explanation: The English drops the directional command or impulse entirely.

findings.highlight: not a place one can stay in human form
findings.evidenceJa: 人の身で存在ていい場所ではない
findings.governingReading: This is not a world where a person is permitted or able to exist in a human body.
findings.explanation: The English changes existential incompatibility into temporary presence while maintaining a form.

findings.governingReading: Each step makes both breathing and further forward movement more difficult.
findings.explanation: The English omits the compounding difficulty of advance.

findings.evidenceJa: 三歩目はとうに不可能
findings.governingReading: A third step has already long since become impossible.
findings.explanation: The English drops the temporal emphasis.

findings.governingReading: The wind continuously shaves or abrades the entire body away.
findings.explanation: The English changes erosion into tearing and drops whole-body scope.

findings.governingReading: The unattainable meter feels like striving toward the farthest extremity of heaven.
findings.explanation: The English mistakes the extreme heavens for an aurora and turns a destination into plural lights.

findings.governingReading: Illya’s call makes Shirou wake with a sudden start.
findings.explanation: The English removes the abrupt transition.

findings.highlight: stare at Illya, standing before me
findings.governingReading: Still dazed, Shirou studies Illya in front of him.
findings.explanation: The English replaces observation with staring and invents that she is standing.

findings.evidenceJa: 先に目が覚めちゃった
findings.governingReading: Illya woke before Shirou and playfully spent the interval observing him.
findings.explanation: The English makes the comparison a clock-time claim.

findings.highlight: I came to look at you
findings.evidenceJa: 観察していたのでしたー
findings.governingReading: Illya playfully announces that she had been observing him.
findings.explanation: The English changes continuing observation into a visit purpose and removes her sing-song register.

findings.highlight: she woke up before me and came here
findings.evidenceJa: 観察してたのはイリヤのが先
findings.governingReading: Shirou notes that Illya had been the first to observe, reversing his own scrutiny.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the observation joke with waking order and arrival.

findings.governingReading: Shirou sets the playful explanation aside to consider her real motive.
findings.explanation: The English makes him personally indifferent.

findings.governingReading: Illya’s intervention has made the pain somewhat easier for the moment.
findings.explanation: The English omits both limited degree and present-time qualification.

findings.highlight: my right hand is on the cloth
findings.evidenceJa: 右手が左腕の布を掴んでいる
findings.governingReading: Shirou discovers his right hand actively gripping the cloth around his left arm.
findings.explanation: The English removes the attempted-removal grip.

findings.evidenceJa: 聖骸布を剥がしてたぞ
findings.governingReading: Without Illya, he concludes he would have stripped off the shroud in his sleep.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the counterfactual outcome into possibility.

findings.governingReading: Shirou thanks Illya for helping him from the morning onward.
findings.explanation: The English omits the time relation.

findings.governingReading: Illya recalls her promise to help when Shirou is suffering.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes bodily or emotional suffering into trouble.

findings.governingReading: Illya’s smile holds Shirou’s gaze for a while.
findings.explanation: The English omits duration.

findings.highlight: just saying that out of kindness
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes Illya’s offer comes from nothing but unalloyed affection.
findings.explanation: “Kindness” removes the personal affection that moves him.

findings.governingReading: Illya’s teasing abruptly brakes the emotional palpitations beginning in Shirou’s chest.
findings.explanation: The English adds panic to a physical and romantic reaction.

findings.evidenceJa: シロウったら可愛いかった
findings.governingReading: Illya teases that Shirou was trying very hard to endure the pain and looked cute.
findings.explanation: The English contains the grammatical typo “your were.”

findings.highlight: the innocence of an adolescent boy at risk
findings.evidenceJa: 思春期の少年のナイーヴな心臓
findings.governingReading: Shirou jokingly frames his own adolescent boy’s sensitive heart as endangered.
findings.explanation: The English sexualizes and moralizes the joke as threatened innocence.

findings.highlight: if she comes close to me in such an outf
findings.evidenceJa: あんな格好で近づかれたら
findings.governingReading: Her crawling close in that posture or clothing risks an embarrassing physiological revelation.
findings.explanation: The English visibly truncates “outfit” and leaves the sentence malformed.

findings.highlight: I hit the back of my head hard
findings.evidenceJa: 後頭部をもろに柱に叩きつけた
findings.governingReading: Shirou strikes the back of his head squarely against a pillar.
findings.explanation: The English omits the pillar.

findings.evidenceJa: ヨロヨロと落ち込みながら
findings.governingReading: He gives the excuse while wobbling and sinking in dejection.
findings.explanation: The English deletes both physical and emotional manner.

findings.governingReading: The impact hurts enough for Shirou to see stars.
findings.explanation: The English adds throbbing rather than retaining the visual pain image.

findings.evidenceJa: ぶんぶん、と頭を振って
findings.governingReading: Shirou shakes his head vigorously before standing.
findings.explanation: The English omits sound and intensity.

findings.governingReading: The shock has completely calmed the ordinary male physiological phenomenon of the morning.
findings.explanation: The English hides the comic bodily referent behind vague “issue.”

findings.highlight: I can cook like everyone else
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he can cook to an ordinary competent degree.
findings.explanation: The English makes the comparison universal and unnatural.

findings.governingReading: Shirou qualifies his ability specifically with Western-style confectionery.
findings.explanation: The English broadens confectionery into snacks.

findings.governingReading: Illya accuses Shirou of already noticing the truth while desperately trying not to notice it.
findings.explanation: The English changes perception and denial into a moralized claim about what he ought to know.

findings.highlight: I know you’ll eventually obtain the magic
findings.evidenceJa: いずれシロウのモノになるとは言っても、今はまだ可能性があるだけ
findings.governingReading: Archer’s magecraft may eventually become Shirou’s, but at present this is only a possibility.
findings.explanation: The English certifies eventual acquisition and weakens the explicit present uncertainty.

findings.governingReading: Shirou blankly repeats Illya’s phrase about what would happen if he attempted Projection.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the repeated warning to the technique’s name.

findings.governingReading: A gunlike firing hammer falls in Shirou’s mind as vague recognition clicks into place.
findings.explanation: “Cocking hammer” is inaccurate mechanical terminology.

findings.governingReading: Shirou provisionally infers reproduction of armaments he has visually perceived.
findings.explanation: The English adds universal “every” and lifetime “ever,” while narrowing armaments to weapons.

findings.governingReading: Illya describes Archer through wrought iron and forging as a distinctive Heroic Spirit.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the epithet to occupation and repeats a malformed noun pile.

findings.governingReading: Illya departs specifically toward the veranda.
findings.explanation: The English omits her destination.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺の体を案じる厳しさ
findings.governingReading: The severity of Illya’s warning contains concern for Shirou’s body.
findings.explanation: The English keeps care but removes its concrete object.

findings.governingReading: Illya’s warning also contains an intent to kill rooted in hatred of Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Hostility” weakens explicit hatred despite retaining murderousness.
